                                          PROJECT NO. 58482

 LARGE LOAD DEMAND                                   §   PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION
 MANAGEMENT SERVICE                                  §                OF TEXAS

       AEP TEXAS INC.’S RESPONSES TO COMMISSION STAFF’S MEMO AND
                         QUESTIONS FOR COMMENT
        AEP Texas Inc. (AEP Texas) respectfully submits these responses to the Public Utility

Commission of Texas (Commission) Staff’s memo and questions for comment regarding large

load demand management service.

1. Of the two options described in the attached slides, an as-needed service or a seasonal service,

    which is the better option to implement PURA § 39.170(b) and why?

AEP Texas does not have any comments at this time but reserves the right to comment in the future.

2. PURA § 39.170(b) states the commission must require ERCOT to develop a reliability service

    to be deployed in the event of an anticipated emergency condition. PURA § 39.170(b)(1) states

    the rules governing the new service must specify the periods when the service may be used to

    assist with maintaining reliability during extreme weather events.

              a. Does PURA authorize ERCOT to deploy the new service in circumstances other

                  than extreme weather events? If yes, what kind of events?

PURA § 39.170(b) contemplates deployment of the service “in the event of an anticipated

emergency condition.” ERCOT protocols define an Energy Emergency Alert as, “an orderly,

predetermined procedure for maximizing use of available Resources and, only if necessary,

curtailing load during an Emergency Condition while providing for the maximum possible

continuity of service and maintaining the integrity of the ERCOT System.”1 In addition, the



        1
            ERCOT Nodal Protocol 2.1, Definitions.

Project No. 58482                                                               AEP Texas’ Responses to
                                                                              Commission Staff Questions
                                                     1
 Railroad Commission regulations include a definition of “energy emergency” as, “any event that

results in firm load shed or has the potential to result in firm load shed required by the reliability

coordinator of a power region in Texas." An event that has the ‘potential to result in firm load shed’

is when the reliability coordinator of a power region in Texas has issued an Energy Emergency

Alert Level 1 or 2.”2

              b. Should the commission define “extreme weather event” and, if so, how should it be

                  defined?

Clarity regarding the definition of “extreme weather event” could serve to mitigate issues

regarding when ERCOT can deploy the large load demand management service. AEP Texas

submits for the Commission’s consideration adoption of a definition of “extreme weather event,”

consistent with the Commission’s definition of “weather emergency,” in the rule for Weather

Emergency Preparedness: “a situation resulting from a summer or winter weather event that

produces significant risk for a [transmission service provider] that firm load must be shed or a

situation for which ERCOT issues an Emergency Notice to market participants involving an

operating condition in which the safety or reliability of the ERCOT system is compromised or

threatened by summer or winter weather.”3

3. PURA § 39.170(b)(3) states the rules governing the new service must prohibit participation by

    any large load customer that curtails in response to the wholesale price of electricity, as

    determined by ERCOT, or that otherwise participates in a different reliability or ancillary

    service. PURA § 37.0561(e)—which allows ERCOT to direct a large load customer with

    onsite backup generation to either curtail its load or deploy its backup generation under certain

Project No. 58482                                                              AEP Texas’ Responses to
                                                                             Commission Staff Questions
                                                       2
     circumstances—states that a large load customer with onsite backup generation may participate

    in a service authorized by PURA § 39.170(b).

            a. What type of qualification is necessary to show that it may take a large load

                customer 24 hours to ramp down safely?

            b. What specific prohibitions not enumerated in PURA § 39.170(b), if any, should

                apply to participation in the new service?

            c. Should participation in price responsiveness to transmission scarcity such as four

                coincident peak (4CP) or a successor methodology preclude participation in the

                new service?

            d. Should the commission define “curtailment in response to wholesale price of

                electricity” and, if so, how should it be defined?

AEP Texas does not have any comments at this time but reserves the right to comment in the future.

4. How should the target quantity, budget, and price be set for the new service?

AEP Texas does not have any comments at this time but reserves the right to comment in the future.

5. What additional information should the Commission consider in its implementation of PURA

    § 39.170(b)?

AEP Texas requests that the Commission consider inclusion of requirements regarding how and

when the list of participating customers will be provided to each applicable transmission and

distribution utility in its implementation of PURA § 39.170(b).

6. PURA §39.170(a) states: The commission shall require the independent organization certified

    under Section 39.151 for the ERCOT power region to ensure that each electric cooperative,

    transmission and distribution utility, and municipally owned utility serving a transmission-

    voltage customer develops a protocol, including the installation of any necessary equipment or



Project No. 58482                                                           AEP Texas’ Responses to
                                                                          Commission Staff Questions
                                                  3
     technology before the customer is interconnected, to allow the load to be curtailed during firm

    load shed. The electric cooperative, transmission and distribution utility, or municipally owned

    utility shall confer with the customer to the extent feasible to shed load in a coordinated

    manner. This subsection applies only to a load interconnected after December 31, 2025, that is

    not: (1) Load operated by a critical load industrial customer, as defined by Section 17.002; or

    (2) Designated as a critical natural gas facility under Section 38.074. Should the Commission

    include in this rulemaking a directive implementing PURA §39.170(a)?

AEP Texas supports inclusion of a directive implementing PURA § 39.170(a) in the instant

rulemaking.

        AEP Texas appreciates the opportunity to provide responses to the questions raised by

Commission Staff. An executive summary of the comments is provided at the end of this filing.
